(2, 5), (5, 8), (8, 11), (11, 14)
Which of the following equations BEST describes the function?
worked_solution: Each ordered pair (x, y) satisfies y = x + 3: 5 = 2+3, 8 = 5+3, 11 = 8+3, 14 = 11+3. stem:
Item 52 refers to the following information regarding the way in which John moves along a straight line for 30 seconds.

For the first 10 seconds, John starts from rest and runs with uniform acceleration. He then runs with constant speed for the next 10 seconds then slowly decreases his speed to arrive at his destination within the final 10 seconds.

Which of the following velocity-time graphs represents John's motion along the straight line?
worked_solution: John's motion has three phases: uniform acceleration from rest for the first 10 seconds (speed rises steadily from 0), constant speed for the next 10 seconds (a horizontal/flat section), then he decreases speed back to rest for the final 10 seconds (speed falls steadily to 0), giving a trapezium shape. Graph A starts already at a constant (non-zero) speed for the first 10 seconds instead of accelerating from rest, then declines - it does not show the initial acceleration phase. Graph C shows speed increasing continuously for the first 20 seconds with no constant-speed section, then falling sharply in the last 10 seconds. Graph B shows the correct pattern: rises for 10 s, constant for 10 s, falls to rest for the final 10 s, matching the description exactly, so B is correct.

stem: If cos A = b/c, which of the following ratios also has the same value as cos A?
worked_solution: By the co-function identity, sin(90° − A) = cos A for any angle A, so sin(90° − A) has the same value as cos A = b/c. cos(90° − A) = sin A, which is generally different from cos A. sin(180° − A) = sin A, also generally different. cos(180° − A) = −cos A, the negative of cos A, not the same value.

stem: A plane is heading in a direction of 045° and changes course clockwise to 135°. The angle through which the plane turns is
In a circle with centre O, the tangent at C forms angles 34° and 74° with chords CA and CB. Which option gives the correct values of p and q?
worked_solution:
For p: angle ACB = 34° is an angle at the circumference subtending arc AB. The angle at the centre standing on the same arc is twice the angle at the circumference, so p = 2(34°) = 68°.

For q: use the alternate segment theorem. The angle between the tangent CF and chord CB is 74°, so angle CAB = 74°. Then in triangle ABC, angle ABC = 180° - 74° - 34° = 72°. By the alternate segment theorem again, the angle between tangent CE and chord CA is also 72°. Since OC is a radius to the point of tangency, OC is perpendicular to EF, so angle ACO = 90° - 72° = 18°. Since OA = OC (radii), triangle AOC is isosceles, so q = angle CAO = angle ACO = 18°.

So p = 68°, q = 18°.
